proposals.title: At the top
proposals.body: I had meant to come down neatly. There was a moment at the top when I still thought I might. I spread both flippers. That made the splash wider.
proposals.review: Strong. Breach and long flippers drive the imagined sequence; splash size and intent are fiction, not a biological explanation of breaching.

proposals.title: Through the middle
proposals.body: Went round underneath them blowing bubbles. They drew together; I came up through the middle. The circle looked so tidy before I put my head through it.
proposals.review: Strong. The visible bubble ring and NOAA-identified feeding tactic supply the event. Competent feeding, no meal frustration or unseen whale partner.

proposals.title: Letting the water out
proposals.body: Came up with my mouth full. Kept the fish behind my baleen and let the water run out. For a little while I was mostly waterfall.
proposals.review: Review. A separate filtering stage with a strong physical image, but the second feeding post may feel less novel after the bubble net. Prey retention is biological context, not prey visibly counted in frame.

proposals.title: Keeping dry
proposals.body: Raised my tail to keep it off the wet sand. Then my head. The middle of me was still cold. I looked over at the others to see whether they had solved this.
proposals.review: Review. Banana posture is visible and species-typical. Cold sensation and consultation are fiction; do not present the joke as the physiological purpose of the posture. Chatham source must be accepted as species-level illustration before admission.

proposals.title: The other view
proposals.body: I woke up looking out to sea. I had gone to sleep facing the glacier. Everyone was still beside me, so I lay my head down again. We could finish turning without my help.
proposals.review: Strong subject to geography review. A drifting ice platform supports the invented rotation; no measured turn or observed sleep sequence is asserted. No pup is assigned to Fenn.

proposals.title: Behind my ear
proposals.body: When I was a pup, I found I could get a hind flipper behind my ear. Reaching it was easy. Staying up on the other flippers took more attention. The itch kept winning.
proposals.review: Strong. Explicit childhood memory and visible self-scratch. Does not imply another pup is scratching her. The image supports the body mechanics; difficulty balancing is imagined.

proposals.title: Who was that for
proposals.body: Someone called from behind me. I lifted my head and answered. So did half the beach. I am fairly sure none of us was the one she wanted.
proposals.review: Review. Raised heads and open mouths support a social calling scene; the actual call and exchange are fiction. Distinct from Fenn posture, but hold if the collective-response joke repeats an admitted episode.

proposals.title: Still going
proposals.body: Caught the wave with the others. It folded under me and I kept going. For a moment my tail was higher than my head. I had not planned a second way of being upside down today.
proposals.review: Strong. Actual airborne arched body, crest and nearby heads support play. Fiction supplies sequence and prior awkwardness; no specific photographed motive is claimed.

proposals.title: One more breath
proposals.body: Lifted my chest to turn over. The pup pressed in underneath me. I stayed up for one more breath, then another. My flippers were beginning to shake before I admitted I was not going anywhere.
proposals.review: Strong. The source explicitly identifies mother and pup, with chest supported and pup pressed against belly. Affection has a concrete bodily cost. Shaking and intention are imagined, not claimed seen.

proposals.title: Across the crest
proposals.body: I took the wave first. She came up beside me before I had cleared it. I stretched out a little farther in the air, which was too late to help but felt necessary.
proposals.review: Strong. Two actual dolphins and an airborne stretched body give the small competition a visible basis. No aerodynamic gain or documented contest is asserted.

proposals.title: Beside me
proposals.body: She came up for air and I came up beside her. On the next breath I was a little ahead. I eased back until I could see her again. Then she went a little faster.
proposals.review: Strong prose, modest image resolution. Close paired surfacing supplies an affectionate race; the second breath and adjustments are fictional sequence. The original published asset is only 549 by 366, not a larger file inferred from a thumbnail.

proposals.title: The inside turn
proposals.body: I let the calf take the inside of the turn. Then I had to swim the long way round to stay beside him. He came out ahead and immediately began another turn.
proposals.review: Review. Adult-and-calf proximity is real; the playful turns are imagined. No motherhood, formal teaching or observed competitive behavior is assigned. Softer 549 by 383 asset requires lead quality approval.
